subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Wuchereria and Brugia: transmission, life cycle, lymphatic disease, diagnosis and treatment
concept: Lymphatic filariasis is a mosquito-borne helminthic infection caused mainly by Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia species.

content.definition: Adult filarial worms inhabit lymphatic vessels while microfilariae circulate in blood.
content.explanation: Mosquitoes acquire microfilariae from infected blood and transmit infective larvae during later bites. Adult worms can cause lymphatic dilation and dysfunction.
content.mechanism: Adult worms and host inflammatory responses damage lymphatic vessels; chronic disease can produce lymphedema, elephantiasis and hydrocele.
content.structure: Major human pathogens include Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi and Brugia timori.
content.function: The vector-host life cycle maintains transmission between infected people and mosquitoes.
causes: Wuchereria bancrofti causes about 90% of global cases
effects: Chronic lymphedema, elephantiasis or hydrocele can develop
content.diagnosis: Blood microscopy for microfilariae and antigen or serologic tests are used according to species and setting.
content.treatment: Treatment and mass drug administration depend on local epidemiology; diethylcarbamazine is used in appropriate settings, while chronic lymphatic damage also needs morbidity management.
high_yield: Wuchereria bancrofti is the major species
Chronic disease may cause elephantiasis and hydrocele

terminology.etymology: Micro means small; filaria refers to thread-like worms.
Refers to marked enlargement resembling an elephant limb.

yemen_context.relevance: Relevant to tropical infectious-disease education; no unsupported Yemen-specific incidence is asserted.

review_notes: Original synthesis based on CDC clinical overview.
